reason: The attentive-similarity model trails baseline SASRec in macro validation HR@10 (0.4725 versus 0.5050) but improves CDs_and_Vinyl (0.5250 versus 0.4800), motivating a test of complementary rankings without assuming complementary errors. Historical mean-rank ensembles support the initial direction, while failed reciprocal-rank and unequal-weight variants favor retaining fixed equal-weight normalized ranks. Modify model_design for the independent experts and shared fusion, and training_evaluation for checkpoint selection, measured ensemble validation, and consistent predictor export.

plan.model_design: Keep AttentiveSimilarity, CausalContextBlock, score_components, forward(history, candidates), predict(history, candidates), its cross-entropy objective, regularization, optimizer, and current hyperparameters unchanged; add the original independent SASRec expert with its supplied architecture, sequence sampler, pointwise positive/negative BCE, Adam optimizer, and baseline defaults. Preserve SASRec.forward(self, seq, pos=None, neg=None) and SASRec.predict(self, seq, candidates), and introduce an ensemble wrapper exposing predict(history, candidates) that prepares each expert's right-aligned chronological history using its saved maxlen. Implement a shared rank_fusion helper that assigns descending zero-based ranks independently to each expert and returns -0.5 * (r_similarity + r_sasrec) / max(candidate_count - 1, 1), preserving the original candidate order and using deterministic item-ID tie-breaking without target-position information. Compute ranks over the entire supplied candidate list, concatenating raw-score chunks before fusion, and give repeated candidate IDs identical ranks so chunk boundaries and duplicate occurrences do not change their relative scores. Keep parameters independent and use the same fixed equal weights for every category, avoiding reciprocal-rank transforms, learned calibration, and category-specific blending to isolate the initial ensemble hypothesis.
plan.training_evaluation: Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], DATASETS, WORKING, train_category(name, device), make_validation(train, valid, itemnum, maxlen), evaluate(model, evaluation, device), and write_predict_script(); extend train_category to train the two experts sequentially on one GPU with separate seed-42 training streams, retaining supplied preprocessing seed 0, unchanged splits, all four routes, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Select each expert independently by validation HR@10 with NDCG@10 breaking ties, save separate strictly loadable checkpoints and actual architecture configurations beneath WORKING, then reload both selected experts and evaluate their fixed ensemble on the same seed-42 validation cases with 200 users per category and 99 unique unseen negatives. Update write_predict_script and check_predictor to load both experts lazily for predict(user_id, history, candidates, *, dataset_name=None), invoke the shared history preparation and full-candidate fusion helpers, and verify checkpoint reload, empty histories, ties, duplicate candidates, candidate permutations, chunk boundaries, and direct-versus-exported score agreement without perturbing training RNG state. Bound both training loops with explicit per-expert deadlines that reserve time for every remaining category, validation, and export within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget, ensuring each expert receives a validated checkpoint before optional further training. Report measured per-category member and ensemble HR@10, optionally their validation hit overlap to assess complementarity, and print the actual four-category ensemble macro-average as Final Validation Score, comparing it with 0.4725 and 0.5050 while leaving the pinned host evaluator and hidden-test inference unchanged.
